claims.citation: New York Herald, 11 May 1866, p. 9, col. 3
claims.verbatim:
Ship Polar Star, West, Liverpool March 9, with mdse, to
Chas Carow. Soon after leaving Liverpool the cargo shift-
ed, giving the ship a considerable list to port. April 6, while
running in a moderate NE gale, vessel was nearly thrown
on her beam ends, carrying away lee bulwarks, head rail,
and started head knees; the cargo shifted so much more that
sail could not be carried on the starboard tack with safety,
and ship could not be kept up to the wind on one tack, or off
it on the other: April 11, took advantage of a calm to exam-
ine the state of cargo, and found that everything had gone
bodily over to port, leaving quite a space on starboard side;
chocked it off with everything available, and then shifted
about 27 tons of tin to starboard, which brought her nearly
upright: the ship did much better afterwards, although in a
stiff breeze would take a list to port or starboard according to
the tack she was on, and labored very heavily, but made no
more water than usual.

Ship Polar Star, West, Liverpool, March 9, with mdse., to Charles
Carow.  (See disasters.)

claims.verbatim:
Ship New World, Ottiwell, Liverpool, 46 days, with mdse
and 42 passengers, to C Grinnell. May 6, lat 44, lon 67 20,
spoke ship Polar Star, from Liverpool for New York.
